evidence: Placebo clinical remission, UC induction trials (meta-analysis to 2014)
detail: Placebo response 33%. Endoscopy subscore 2 or more at entry lowered placebo rates; longer trials and more visits raised them.
source: Jairath et al., J Crohns Colitis 2016

evidence: Placebo clinical remission, UC induction trials (meta-analysis 2014-2020)
detail: Absence of central endoscopy reading raised placebo endoscopic rates; more follow-up visits and longer trials raised clinical placebo rates.
source: Sedano et al., J Crohns Colitis 2022

evidence: Placebo clinical remission, East Asian UC induction trials
detail: Placebo endoscopic remission 26%. Relevant because the trial runs in mainland China, Taiwan, Korea and Australia.
source: Meta-analysis of East Asian UC RCTs, 2022

evidence: Tofacitinib phase 2, among the strongest UC phase 2 results
detail: Week-8 remission at 10-15 mg twice daily; clinical response 78% vs 42%. The protocol's 40% assumption sits at this level.

evidence: IL-6 antibody PF-04236921 in Crohn's disease (ANDANTE)
detail: Week-12 remission at 50 mg. Gastrointestinal abscess and perforation were observed; the 200 mg dose was stopped for safety.
Clinical remission on the 3-item modified Mayo score with a centrally read endoscopy subscore; the physician global assessment is dropped.
source: FDA, Ulcerative Colitis: Developing Drugs for Treatment, 2022
